evidence.text: the original at 0x289bc holds 117 instructions and 415 bytes up to the ret at 0x28b5a. The first loop walks the signed source DAT_00102108 and stops at the first negative entry. A source entry with the value 0 or with a clear byte at DAT_00100002[i] clears the flag DAT_00120884[i] and moves the value into the queue DAT_0012082c through the count DAT_0012087c. The queue write also clears the next slot. A source entry above 0 with a set byte at DAT_00100002[i] sets the flag to 1 and waits. The count stops at 4, so the queue holds five entries. The second loop walks the nine 0x18-byte records at DAT_00102e04 with the five-byte key at +0, the value pointer at +0xc, the value at +0x10, and the xor flag at +0x14. It compares the low byte of each of the five queue entries and stops at a zero queue entry without a mismatch. It runs the record on a full match with a store or an xor through the pointer. It calls table_lookup at 0x1f718 with 8 and clears the count and the first queue entry. It clears the queue when all nine records mismatch.
